blueprint_topic: Management of Care — discharge reconciliation, multidisciplinary collaboration, referrals, plan-of-care updating, and handoff
stem: A client with advanced liver disease is preparing for discharge. The hepatology, nutrition, and social-work plans contain different follow-up instructions, and the client is unsure which appointments and referrals are required. Which action by the nurse best supports continuity of care?

options.A: Reconcile the differing plans with the involved disciplines, clarify unresolved orders or referrals, update discharge instructions, and provide an accurate handoff.
options.B: Give the client each discipline's current instructions and advise calling the clinics later if conflicts remain, so discharge is not delayed by reconciliation.
options.C: Use the hepatology instructions as the primary discharge plan and ask nutrition and social work to reconcile their differing recommendations at later follow-up visits.
options.D: Complete insurance and transportation arrangements first, then leave unresolved clinical referrals for the outpatient team to clarify after discharge.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan places handoff, multidisciplinary collaboration, provider-order verification, referral assessment, plan-of-care updating, and resource utilization within Management of Care. When discharge instructions conflict, the nurse should help reconcile the plan with the involved disciplines, clarify unresolved orders/referrals, update the discharge plan, and ensure an accurate handoff rather than passing contradictions downstream. B is incorrect because knowingly handing the client conflicting instructions without reconciliation undermines continuity and safe discharge planning. C is incorrect because selecting one discipline's plan as primary and deferring reconciliation leaves known multidisciplinary discrepancies unresolved at discharge. D is incorrect because insurance and transportation coordination can be important, but administrative tasks do not replace reconciliation of unresolved clinical referrals and follow-up instructions before discharge.
educational_objective: Coordinate complex discharge care by reconciling multidisciplinary recommendations, clarifying unresolved orders and referrals, updating the discharge plan, and providing an accurate handoff so the client receives a coherent follow-up plan.

correction_summary: Rebuilt all four alternatives to remove the original extreme correct-answer length cue and absolute-word distractor pattern. Post-fetch adversarial reread replaced an overly obvious specialty-plan deletion distractor with the more realistic error of privileging one discipline's plan and deferring reconciliation. The final choices test interdisciplinary reconciliation, passing conflicts downstream, single-service primacy, and administrative-only coordination.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches NCSBN Management-of-Care activities for collaboration, order/referral clarification, plan updating, and handoff.
option_audit.B: Plausible workflow-pressure error; incorrect because unresolved conflicting instructions should not simply be handed to the client for later clarification.
option_audit.C: Plausible single-service primacy error; incorrect because known multidisciplinary discrepancies should be reconciled rather than deferred to later specialty visits.
option_audit.D: Plausible administrative-priority error; incorrect because administrative coordination does not substitute for resolving clinical referrals and follow-up instructions before discharge.
